name: MinimizeCrashInput
prose: Driver function in FuzzerDriver.cpp. If Inputs does not hold exactly one path it prints an error and calls exit(1). It builds BaseCmd from Args with the minimize_crash and exact_artifact_path flags and the input path removed (assert that the path is an argument), adds -max_total_time=600 when Flags.runs <= 0 and Flags.max_total_time == 0, and merges the child's stdout and stderr. Then it loops: it reads the current file, runs the command on it through ExecuteCommand (which returns true when the child exits with status 0; a failed popen also yields false); if the run returns true (child exited 0, i.e. no crash) it prints 'did not crash' and calls exit(1). Otherwise it records the first dedup token from the output, runs the command again with minimize_crash_internal_step=1 and exact_artifact_path set to Flags.exact_artifact_path or a 'minimized-from-<hash>' path under the artifact prefix. If that second run returns true (the child exited 0, which this code reports as 'failed to minimize beyond'), it sets CurrentFilePath and rewrites the original bytes there only when Flags.exact_artifact_path is set, and leaves the loop; the function then returns 0. If the second run exits nonzero it compares dedup tokens: if they differ it again (when exact_artifact_path is set) writes U to that path and breaks out of the loop, so the function returns 0; if equal it continues with the new artifact path as the current input. The only return is 0 after a break; exit(1) is used for the other failures.
note: Round-15 reviewer right: 'Success' is ExecuteCommand's true = child exit status 0 (FuzzerUtilPosix.cpp: pclose(Pipe) == 0), so the break means the internal step ended without a crash, not that the input stopped crashing. Original reviewer right on the exit(1) path and break conditions; old prose was ambiguous.

name: operator new(size_t, nothrow_t const&)
prose: C++ allocation operator (nothrow), compiled when HWASAN_REPLACE_OPERATORS_NEW_AND_DELETE is set (the aligned forms exist only under that condition). It captures a malloc stack trace (GET_MALLOC_STACK_TRACE) and returns hwasan_malloc(size, &stack) directly, with no ReportOutOfMemory call of its own. The result is null only if the hwasan allocator returned null, which happens for a failing request (too large, RSS limit, out of memory) only when the allocator is allowed to return null (allocator_may_return_null; errno is also set on null); otherwise the allocator itself reports the error and does not return. A non-null result is released with operator delete. In the alternative __ANDROID__ configuration (when HWASAN_REPLACE_OPERATORS_NEW_AND_DELETE is not set) the body is instead 'return malloc(size)'.
note: Round-15 reviewer wrong for the nothrow forms (OPERATOR_NEW_BODY_*_NOTHROW, hwasan_new_delete.cpp:31-33,40-42,49-51,58-60 call hwasan_malloc/hwasan_memalign and return it with no report); the old prose 'nothing is reported' was too strong because the allocator reports unless allocator_may_return_null. For the non-nothrow aligned forms the old prose was already correct, reviewer wrong.

name: InternalGetProcAddress
prose: Windows PE export-table lookup in interception_win.cpp. It builds RVAPtr views over module and reads dos_stub->e_lfanew while constructing headers, before the '!module' test in the following if, so a null module is dereferenced there (undefined behavior) rather than returning 0. The following check returns 0 if module is null (only meaningful if the dereference above did not fault), if e_magic is not 'MZ', if the NT signature is wrong, or if SizeOfOptionalHeader is smaller than sizeof(IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER); it returns 0 if the export directory size is 0, and 0 after scanning NumberOfNames names without any equal to func_name. For the first name equal to func_name it takes the ordinal-indexed function RVA: if that RVA lies inside the export directory (a forwarder string 'module.function') it copies the string into a 256-byte buffer, splits at the first '.', calls GetModuleHandleA on the module part and returns the recursive InternalGetProcAddress(redirected_module, text after the '.'); if the forwarder string is 255 or more characters, has no '.', or GetModuleHandleA returns null, it calls ReportError and InterceptionFailed (which prints and executes __debugbreak; it is not declared noreturn, so with a debugger attached execution can continue past it). Otherwise it returns the in-memory address (module base + RVA) of the function as uptr.
note: Reviewers (rounds 1, 15) right about the null-module dereference; round 2 partially right: InterceptionFailed does report and __debugbreak() (interception_win.cpp:164-169) but is not noreturn, so it is not guaranteed to leave the function.

name: INTERCEPTORS_STRTO_BASE(long, strtol, char)
prose: Generated interceptor: macro INTERCEPTORS_STRTO_BASE(long, strtol, char) expands INTERCEPTOR_STRTO_BASE, defining long strtol(const char *nptr, char **endptr, int base) (and, from the same macro, the strtol_l variants: strtol_l, plus __strtol_l except on NetBSD). The body is INTERCEPTOR_STRTO_BODY: ENSURE_MSAN_INITED(), then res = REAL(strtol)(nptr, endptr, base), then __msan_unpoison(endptr, sizeof(*endptr)), then return res. __msan_unpoison returns without effect if the address is not in application memory (a null endptr is thus ignored). The parsed value is returned unchanged; nptr is not checked here.
note: Previously dropped for 'name not in slice'; the function is macro-generated (msan_interceptors.cpp:463-467, 527), so fixed under the macro invocation.

name: ELFNixPlatformRuntimeState::dlopenFull
prose: Member function taking std::unique_lock<std::recursive_mutex> &JDStateLock (held on entry, by the caller's convention) and PerJITDylibState &JDS. It first calls JDStateLock.unlock(), then calls the push-initializers wrapper through JITDispatch with JDS.Header; if that call itself returns an error it returns that error with the lock still unlocked. Otherwise it re-locks JDStateLock; if DepInfo holds an error it returns that error (lock held); otherwise it calls dlopenInitialize(JDStateLock, JDS, *DepInfo) and returns its error if any (dlopenInitialize and runInits only unlock temporarily around calling initializers and re-lock before returning); if the dep-info map is still non-empty afterwards it returns a StringError 'Encountered unrecognized dep-info key headers while processing dlopen of <name>' (lock held); else it returns Error::success() with the lock held.
note: Both reviewers right: the early wrapper-call error returns with the lock released (elfnix_platform.cpp:477-481), and the success-wrapper-call path can still return an error from DepInfo or from leftover dep-info keys (lines 484-496).

name: MachOPlatformRuntimeState::dlopenFull
prose: Member function taking std::unique_lock<std::mutex> &JDStatesLock (held on entry by the caller's convention) and JITDylibState &JDS. It unlocks JDStatesLock, calls the push-initializers wrapper through JITDispatch with JDS.Header and, if that call returns an error, returns it with the lock still unlocked. Otherwise it re-locks; if DepInfo holds an error it returns that error (lock held); then it calls dlopenInitialize(JDStatesLock, JDS, *DepInfo) and returns its error if any; if the dep-info map is still non-empty it logs under ORC_RT_DEBUG and returns a StringError 'Encountered unrecognized dep-info key headers while processing dlopen of <name>'; otherwise it returns Error::success(). Whether JDS is sealed or unsealed is handled inside dlopenInitialize (sealed JITDylibs with a non-empty dependency list produce an error there, sealed already-referenced ones are skipped); this function does not test it.
note: Old preconditions (unsealed or first-time) are not checked in this function; rewritten from macho_platform.cpp:1083-1115 and dlopenInitialize 1117-1186.

name: MachOPlatformRuntimeState::dlupdateFull
prose: Member function taking std::unique_lock<std::mutex> &JDStatesLock (held on entry by the caller's convention) and JITDylibState &JDS (dlupdateImpl only calls it for an unsealed, referenced JITDylib; this function does not check that). It unlocks JDStatesLock, calls the push-initializers wrapper through JITDispatch with JDS.Header and returns that call's error, with the lock still unlocked, if it fails. Otherwise it re-locks; if DepInfo holds an error it returns it (lock held); otherwise it calls dlupdateInitialize(JDStatesLock, JDS), which runs registerObjCRegistrationObjects and runModInits for JDS only, and returns an error from it if any, else Error::success(). The contents of a successful DepInfo are not used.
note: Old prose said dlupdateInitialize 're-ran initializers' and did not mention that DepInfo's value is ignored; rewritten from macho_platform.cpp:1211-1247.

name: __llvm_write_custom_profile
prose: Function in InstrProfilingFile.c (compiled when __APPLE__ is not defined); the slice cut the head. It saves the current profile file with getProfileFile() as oldFile and calls lprofSuspendSigKill() (PDeathSig). Return paths: (1) if lprofProfileDumped() or continuous mode is enabled, it prints a note, calls lprofRestoreSigKill() when PDeathSig == 1 and returns 0; (2) if the runtime profile version does not match INSTR_PROF_RAW_VERSION it prints an error, restores SIGKILL and returns -1; (3) if getCurFilename gives no filename it prints an error, restores SIGKILL and returns -1; (4) otherwise it builds, in alloca'd buffers, the target-specific name by inserting 'Target.' before the basename of the current filename, calls fopen(name, "w") and setProfileFile(OutputFile) before checking the result; if fopen failed it prints an error, restores SIGKILL and returns -1, leaving the registered profile file as NULL (oldFile is not restored); (5) on success it sets FreeHook to free, calls setupIOBuffer(), initializes a file writer, takes Version from __llvm_profile_get_version() unless *VersionOverride is supplied (VersionOverride non-NULL), calls lprofWriteDataImpl(...) and stores its result, closes the file with closeFileObject, restores SIGKILL if PDeathSig == 1, restores the saved profile file with setProfileFile(oldFile) and returns lprofWriteDataImpl's result (nonzero value signals a write failure as defined by that function). Target is used with strlen (must be a NUL-terminated string).
note: Name from source (slice cut the head; the old name writeTargetProfileFile does not exist anywhere under compiler-rt). Prose follows InstrProfilingFile.c:1280-1387; the old prose was consistent with this except that it asserted lprofWriteDataImpl returns 0 or negative.

name: parseFilenamePattern
prose: Static function in InstrProfilingFile.c. It frees lprofCurFilename.ProfilePathPrefix if set, frees lprofCurFilename.FilenamePat if owned, then memset-zeroes the whole lprofCurFilename structure (so PNS, TmpDir, MergePoolSize, NumPids/NumHosts/NumBinaryIds and others are reset to 0), and stores FilenamePat in it: the caller's pointer when CopyFilenamePat is 0, otherwise strdup(FilenamePat) with OwnsFilenamePat = 1 (no check that strdup succeeded). It then scans the pattern, handling each '%x': %p stores the pid text on the first occurrence (return -1 with a warning if snprintf returns <= 0); %h gets the hostname on the first occurrence (return -1 if gethostname fails); %t reads TMPDIR into TmpDir on each occurrence (return -1 if unset); %b on the first occurrence checks that __llvm_write_binary_ids(NULL) > 0 (return -1 otherwise); %c returns -1 after disabling continuous mode if it is already enabled, otherwise enables continuous mode and sets the page size on Mach-O/ELF/COFF/AIX targets and returns -1 on other targets; any other character goes to getMergePoolSize: if it is a %m / %Nm specifier a second one returns -1, the first sets MergePoolSize, and a non-m character is skipped. At the end it stores NumPids, NumHosts and NumBinaryIds and returns 0. On every -1 return the new pattern is already stored, the three counts are still 0, and TmpDir, MergePoolSize or continuous mode may already have been set by earlier specifiers.
note: Round-15 reviewer right: the memset zeroes PNS as well, so the old 'leaving PNS untouched' was wrong. Rounds 1 and 2 wrong: the prose already listed the duplicate-%m and unsupported-%c returns and the success path copying the three counts (InstrProfilingFile.c:842-876).

name: RoundUp
prose: Static function (compiled only when NT_GNU_BUILD_ID is defined) in InstrProfilingPlatformLinux.c: returns (size + align - 1) & ~(align - 1) as size_t, with unsigned wraparound if size + align - 1 exceeds the size_t range. For align a power of two this is the smallest multiple of align that is at least size (when no wraparound occurs); for an align that is not a power of two the expression does not round to a multiple of align. No memory is read or written.
note: Contract cleared (reviewers right: the formal used UINT64_MAX instead of SIZE_MAX, a 64-bit-only bound, and omitted minimality). Source line 125-127.

name: TEST(TestRtsanInterceptors, IoctlBehavesWithOutputPointer)
prose: gtest test (macro TEST, body is TestBody of TestRtsanInterceptors_IoctlBehavesWithOutputPointer_Test). It opens an AF_INET stream socket; if that returns -1 it prints the error and GTEST_SKIP()s (returns from the body). It calls getifaddrs; if that returns -1 or a null list it prints the error, closes the socket and skips. Otherwise it zero-initializes an ifreq and copies the first interface's name (strncpy, at most IFNAMSIZ-1 bytes) into it and calls ioctl(sock, SIOCGIFADDR, &ifr). If ioctl returns -1 it prints the error, closes the socket, frees the list and FAIL()s. Otherwise it frees the list, closes the socket and makes two fatal assertions: ifr_addr.sa_data is not null (an array member, so its address is always non-null) and ifr_addr.sa_family equals AF_INET. It returns nothing.
note: Checked against rtsan_test_interceptors_posix.cpp:788-821.

name: pthread_create (INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_create, pthread_t *thread, const pthread_attr_t *attr, void *(*start_routine)(void*), void *arg))
prose: Interceptor defined with INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_create, ...) in safestack.cpp (named pthread_create, not pthread_create_interceptor). It calls EnsureInterceptorsInitialized(), then obtains size and guard (both initially 0): if attr is non-null from pthread_attr_getstacksize and pthread_attr_getguardsize on attr, otherwise from a temporary default pthread_attr_t initialized and destroyed locally; the return values of the getters are not checked, so a failing getter leaves the value at 0. On Solaris a size of 0 is replaced with 2 MiB (LP64) or 1 MiB. SFS_CHECK(size) then aborts the process (fprintf and abort) if size is 0. size is rounded up to 16; unsafe_stack_alloc(size, guard) aborts if size+guard overflows or mmap fails, mprotect-s the guard area PROT_NONE and returns the address after the guard. A struct tinfo is placed at the end of that mapping holding start_routine, arg and the stack parameters. The function returns REAL(pthread_create)(thread, attr, thread_start, tinfo) directly: on success the new thread runs thread_start, which installs the unsafe stack (and so overwrites tinfo's contents) and calls start_routine(arg); the stack is released later by the thread-exit cleanup handler. If the real pthread_create fails, its error code is returned and the mapped unsafe stack (which contains tinfo) is not unmapped, so it is leaked.
note: Slice cut the head: the function is INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_create, ...). Old prose wrong in claiming getter failures are returned (lines 240-250 ignore them; failure leads to SFS_CHECK abort or a default value) and that tinfo is a separate allocation (it lives inside the mapped stack, lines 269-270). Reviewer round 1 right on the leak, which the old prose already stated.

name: AddrHashMap<T, kSize>::Handle::Handle(AddrHashMap<T, kSize> *map, uptr addr)
prose: Handle constructor (template member): sets map_ = map, addr_ = addr, remove_ = false and create_ = true, then calls map_->acquire(this), which sets created_, addidx_, bucket_ and cell_. Because create_ is true and remove_ false, acquire leaves cell_ non-null: either an existing cell (found lock-free in the bucket's embedded cells with no lock held, or in the bucket's add array with the bucket read lock held and addidx_ set), or a newly claimed cell with created_ true, addr still 0 and the bucket's exclusive lock held until the destructor (release) publishes the address. It returns nothing; the destructor calls map_->release(this).
note: Round-15 reviewer wrong for this constructor: create_ is true here, so cell_ cannot be null (sanitizer_addrhashmap.h:140-146 and acquire lines 285-331).

name: AddrHashMap<T, kSize>::Handle::Handle(AddrHashMap<T, kSize> *map, uptr addr, bool remove)
prose: Handle constructor (template member): sets map_ = map, addr_ = addr, remove_ = remove and create_ = true, then calls map_->acquire(this). If remove is false the outcome is that of the two-argument constructor (non-null cell_: existing cell with no lock or the bucket read lock, or a new cell with created_ true and the exclusive bucket lock held). If remove is true, acquire skips the lock-free search, takes the bucket's exclusive lock and, if a cell for addr exists, sets cell_ to it (created_ false) and keeps the lock; if none exists it releases the lock and leaves cell_ null (exists() is false). The destructor (release) then removes the cell and unlocks. It returns nothing.
note: Round-15 reviewer wrong for this constructor: with create_ true the only null-cell case is remove=true, which the old prose already stated.

name: AddrHashMap<T, kSize>::Handle::Handle(AddrHashMap<T, kSize> *map, uptr addr, bool remove, bool create)
prose: Handle constructor (template member): sets map_, addr_, remove_ and create_ from the arguments and calls map_->acquire(this). With remove true: acquire takes the bucket's exclusive lock; cell_ is the existing cell for addr (created_ false, lock held until the destructor removes it and unlocks) or null if none exists (lock released). With remove false: an existing cell is found lock-free in the embedded cells (no lock held) or in the add array (bucket read lock held, addidx_ set), after a retry loop that also covers a cell inserted concurrently; if none exists and create is true, a new cell is claimed with created_ true and the bucket's exclusive lock held until the destructor publishes it; if none exists and create is false, cell_ is null, created_ is false and no lock is held. It returns nothing.
note: Round-15 reviewer right for this constructor: remove=false, create=false and absent address leaves cell_ null; the old prose omitted that case.

name: AddrHashMap<T, kSize>::acquire
prose: Member function of AddrHashMap (declared SANITIZER_NO_THREAD_SAFETY_ANALYSIS) that fills in Handle *h: it sets h->created_ = false, addidx_ = -1U, bucket_ = the bucket for hash(addr_) and cell_ = nullptr. The calling thread must not already hold that bucket's mutex. If remove_ is false it first looks lock-free in the bucket's embedded cells (found: cell_ set, nothing locked, return); then, if the bucket has an add array, it takes the read lock and scans it (found: addidx_ and cell_ set, read lock held, return; not found: read lock released). It then takes the exclusive lock and re-checks the embedded cells and the add array: if the address is found and remove_ is set it sets cell_ (and addidx_ for the add array) and returns holding the exclusive lock; if it is found and remove_ is not set (it appeared concurrently) it unlocks and goes back to the lock-free search again. If it is not found and remove_ is set or create_ is false, it unlocks and returns with cell_ null. Otherwise it sets created_ = true and claims a free embedded cell (addidx_ stays -1U) or, in the add array, a new slot at index add->size (allocating a 64-byte array with InternalAlloc the first time, or doubling it with InternalAlloc/memcpy/InternalFree when full), setting addidx_ and cell_; it returns with the exclusive lock held and the cell's addr still 0 (release() publishes it). It returns nothing.
note: Round-15 reviewer wrong: the old prose already said absent-and-remove_ gives null (lines 284-288). Round-17 reviewer right in a narrow sense: the retry (unlock and search again when a non-removing lookup finds the element under the exclusive lock, lines 256-263 and 272-280) was not in the old prose; the lock-free add-array hit does return holding the read lock (lines 234-244).

name: SizeClassAllocator32<Params>::ClassID
prose: Static member function of the 32-bit primary allocator: returns SizeClassMap::ClassID(size). In SizeClassMap::ClassID, size greater than kMaxSize gives 0; size up to kMidSize gives (size + kMinSize - 1) >> kMinSizeLog, which is 0 for size 0 and at least 1 for size from 1; larger sizes give kMidClass + (l1 << S) + hbits + (lbits > 0), computed from the most-significant-bit index of size. So the result is 0 for size 0 and for size above kMaxSize, and nonzero for sizes from 1 to kMaxSize. It reads no mutable state.
note: Round-15 reviewer right (size 0 gives 0, sanitizer_allocator_size_class_map.h:158-162). Round-2 reviewer wrong: sizes above kMaxSize are handled (return 0), so there is no precondition. Upper bound by kNumClasses dropped as not verified from this code alone.

name: TgKill
prose: Function in sanitizer_linux.cpp whose body depends on the platform macro: on Linux it returns internal_syscall(SYSCALL(tgkill), pid, tid, sig), the raw kernel return (0 on success or a negative errno value); on FreeBSD it returns internal_syscall(SYSCALL(thr_kill2), pid, tid, sig), where internal_syscall maps to libc syscall/__syscall, so failure is -1 with errno set rather than -errno; on Solaris it ignores pid, assigns errno = thr_kill(tid, sig) and returns -1 if errno is then nonzero, otherwise 0; on Haiku it ignores pid and sig and returns kill_thread(tid), the status_t result. No arguments are validated.
note: Old prose wrong for FreeBSD (said -errno): sanitizer_syscall_generic.inc defines internal_syscall as syscall/__syscall there. Round-15 reviewer wrong: thr_kill returns the error number (stored into errno, then -1 is returned), as the prose said for Solaris.

name: ThreadDescriptorSizeFallback
prose: Static function in sanitizer_linux_libcdep.cpp; the file has two definitions of this name, one for SANITIZER_GLIBC and one for SANITIZER_FREEBSD (both without SANITIZER_GO), and the slice contains the FreeBSD one in full. The FreeBSD one takes no arguments and, depending on the compile-time architecture macros, returns: on s390 or sparc 524 (32-bit) or 1552 (64-bit); on mips 1152 (32-bit) or 1776 (64-bit); on loongarch64 1856; on aarch64 1776; on powerpc64 1776; and 0 if none of those macros is defined. The glibc definition (lines 224-296) returns a version-dependent size on x86, arm (reads gnu_get_libc_version and aborts via CHECK_EQ if the major version is not 2), values 1772 or 1936 on riscv64 depending on the glibc minor version, and the same constants as the FreeBSD one on s390/sparc/mips/loongarch64/aarch64/powerpc64; the glibc one has no final return for an unlisted architecture.
note: Both reviewers (rounds 1, 2, 15) right about the earlier formal contract (cleared); the file has two definitions, the riscv64 values belong to the glibc one (sanitizer_linux_libcdep.cpp lines 260-268), which the old prose did not mention.

name: internal_ftruncate
prose: NetBSD definition in sanitizer_netbsd.cpp (fd_t fd, uptr size): CHECK(&__ftruncate) aborts if the __ftruncate symbol is unavailable, then HANDLE_EINTR(res, __ftruncate(fd, 0, (s64)size)) calls it repeatedly while it fails with errno EINTR, and the function returns res as uptr: 0 on success or (uptr)-1 with errno set on another failure. EINTR is never returned. size is cast to s64, so sizes above INT64_MAX become negative lengths passed to the system call.
